section_summary.extract_value: The abstract reports a single empirical study (Study X) using a sample of 490 women that tested whether early positive memories are negatively associated with disordered eating via social safeness and body appreciation, controlling for BMI. The path model explained 51% of variance in eating psychopathology and identified social safeness and body appreciation as mediators of the effect of early warm and safe memories on disordered eating.
section_summary.evidence_source: "Using a sample of 490 women, the hypothesis that early positive memories are negatively associated with disordered eating via social safeness and a positive relationship with one's body image was tested via path analysis. The tested model explained 51% of eating psychopathology's variance, and revealed a good adjustment to the empirical data. Additionally, social safeness and body appreciation were revealed as mediators of the impact of early warm and safe memories on disordered eating, when controlling for the effect of BMI."
